verified_rules: title plans support the property description in the register and identify the general extent of registered land
title plans and registers must be read together with referenced filed documents
all title plans show general boundaries unless a boundary is determined under section 60 of the Land Registration Act 2002
a determined boundary records an exact line only after that line has already been identified; HMLR does not resolve the underlying disagreement
the determined-boundary plan must identify start end and turning points and include a descriptive statement
the preferred determined-boundary plan scale is no smaller than 1:200
ordinary title-plan scales are usually 1:1250 urban and 1:2500 rural, with 1:5000 or 1:10000 possible for large rural areas
deed-derived dimensions do not convert a general boundary into an exact boundary and may become unreliable when reference features change
the title plan was updated on 13 July 2026 to add a brace-reference example
general-boundary red edging carries a zone of uncertainty and cannot be promoted to surveyed parcel geometry
quality_gate: PASS for registry semantics; BLOCKED for exact candidate polygon and measured boundary
